title: Laboratory Technician Supervisor
description:
About Us: Founded in 2004 by local physicians, Animas Surgical Hospital has been an integral part of the Four Corners region for more than two decades. Our goal has never been to be the only hospital in Durango but to be the best option for surgery, diagnostic imaging, emergency care, occupational medicine, and internal medicine.

Our Mission: To provide innovative, exceptional healthcare that patients recommend, physicians prefer, and employees are proud of.

Job Title: Laboratory Technician Supervisor

Job Summary: Responsible for coordination and management of in-house lab operations.

Reports To: Director, Outpatient Services

Hourly Range: $26.83 to $40.91 (posted hourly range excludes overtime and bonuses which are not guaranteed)

Essential Job Functions:

Under the supervision of the Lab Technical Consultant and Department Director, performs and coordinates all in-house lab testing and coordination.

  • Performs testing and analysis
  • Responsible for collecting, logging, and transferring all laboratory specimens, including cultures and pathology
  • Coordinates API testing at direction of Technical Consultant
  • Ensures accuracy and maintenance of competency and proficiency testing records and documentation
  • Ensures accuracy and maintenance of documentation of QC and validation studies
  • Identifies problems that may adversely affect testing or reporting of result
  • Investigates reported or identified lab deficiencies or issues
  • Oversees and manages lab supply and inventory tracking
  • Works with ASH clinical departments, lab personnel, and contracted lab services to optimize specimen workflow.
  • Responsible for Quality Assurance Program in the lab
  • Management of Blood Bank
  • Responsible for supply distribution and quality control

Additional Duties

  • Performs other duties as assigned.
  • Demonstrates the spirit of the philosophy, mission, and values of the hospital through words and actions, and implements them into departmental processes, programs, and the working environment.

Minimum Requirements

Education Bachelor's degree with a CLS or MLT certification. Associates degree in an applied science field meeting CLIA's general supervisor qualification.

Experience: Minimum 1 year experience working in a high complexity laboratory. Experience with managing personnel and processes.

Physical Requirements

Position regularly requires use of hands to finger, handle or feel; reach with hands and arms. Must be able to stand, walk, sit, stoop, kneel and crouch. Must be able to lift up to 25 pounds. Must be able to use computer keyboard and mouse and lab instrumentation. Specific vision abilities required include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, and depth perception.

Working Conditions/Environmental Exposures

Environmental hazards such as chemicals, solvents, needles, needle containers, sharps, blood, body fluids, various infectious/communicable diseases, infectious medical waste, radiation, and/or radioactive materials and/or radioactive waste, proximity to moving mechanical parts. Protective clothing/equipment may be necessary.

Animas Health Immunizations and Vaccinations Requirements

Aligns with CDC’s Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) for Healthcare Personnel

  • Hepatitis B- Lab evidence of immunity (titer) to Hepatitis B or three doses Hep B vaccine at appropriate intervals
  • Influenza- documentation of current seasonal flu vaccine (mandatory from November 1st through March 31st each year)
  • Measles, Mumps, and Rubella - Lab evidence of immunity (titer) to Measles, Mumps, and Rubella or 2 doses of MMR Vaccination
  • Varicella (chickenpox) - Lab evidence of immunity (titer) to Varicella or 2 doses of Varicella Vaccine
  • Tetanus, diphtheria, pertussis (Tdap) - documented proof of immunization
  • Tuberculosis Screening - Documentation of a two-step TB skin test within the past year OR lab verification of a negative TB Gold or T-Spot tuberculin test within the past 6 months

*Vaccine records or evidence of immunity are required prior to 1st day of scheduled work.

Animas Health is a drug free workplace and performs a pre-employment drug screen which includes marijuana.

We Offer Competitive Pay and Benefits

Employment with us provides competitive salaries and a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your health, financial well-being, and professional growth.

Eligible employees enjoy:

  • Health, Vision and Dental insurance
  • Life insurance
  • Paid Time Off
  • 401(k) plan with employer match
  • Education and Tuition benefits
  • Flexible Spending and Health Savings accounts
  • Additional optional benefits

title: IT Business Partner
description:
Overview

Trinseo is a different kind of global materials company – at the intersection of people, technology, and customers. We are a world leader in the production of plastics and latex binders. Our culture is built on passion and innovation.

A career at Trinseo presents a unique opportunity to work in a highly collaborative environment. Helping customers solve their most complex material challenges is the reason we come to work each day. We are seeking innovative thinkers – ready to tackle any challenge and passionate about delivering value.

As a global materials solutions provider focused on delivering innovative and sustainable solutions to our customers, we need people to feel respected and included so they can be more creative, innovative, and successful. We strive to create workplaces that reflect all communities and customers we serve and where everyone feels empowered to bring their full, authentic selves to work. That's why we're fully committed to inclusion across race, gender, age, religion, identity, and experience to drive us forward every day.

Overview (Scope of Role)

The IT Business Partner serves as the strategic relationship owner, primary point of contact, and IT planning lead for assigned Finance, Payroll, and Corporate business stakeholders. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in a fast-paced, global, and transformational environment and enjoys connecting business priorities with practical, value-driven technology solutions.

Working closely with the SAP Finance team and broader IT organization, the IT Business Partner ensures business priorities, process improvement opportunities, and technology needs are translated into actionable IT roadmaps and delivery plans. The role is responsible for the intake, assessment, prioritization, implementation, and value realization of technology initiatives across Trinseo's Finance and Corporate application landscape, including Treasury, Fixed Assets, Cost Accounting, FP&A, Tax, Internal Audit, Internal Controls, and Payroll.

The successful candidate will bring functional familiarity with SAP Finance processes and related technologies such as Concur, BlackLine, ONESOURCE, IT2, and Power BI. They will be outcome-oriented, comfortable operating in ambiguity, and capable of leveraging AI technologies as productivity and insight enablers.

The role works closely with business stakeholders, IT teams, and external solution providers to define requirements, align technology capabilities with business objectives, support delivery and adoption, and drive continuous improvement in systems, processes, and user experience.

This will be a hybrid position in Wayne, PA

title: Marketing Data Analyst
description:
Position Purpose

Upholds the Credit Union’s mission of “We do the right thing one member, one employee, and one experience at a time to strengthen the communities we serve” by providing objective, data-driven analysis of marketing strategies, campaigns, channels, and investments to improve decision-making and maximize business impact.

The Marketing Data Analyst is an important role within the Data Services department partnering closely with Marketing and other areas of the Credit Union. This role serves as the subject matter expert for marketing analytics and measurement, using member, transactional, campaign, digital, and other available data to determine what is working, what is not, and where opportunities exist.

This role goes beyond reporting marketing activity by evaluating the effectiveness and business impact of marketing efforts. The Marketing Data Analyst is expected to exercise independent analytical judgment, challenge assumptions when appropriate, and clearly communicate conclusions based on evidence — including when findings differ from expectations or established perspectives.

Essential Responsibilities

  • Marketing Performance & Measurement: Own the measurement of marketing campaigns, channels, and investments, including KPIs, attribution, ROI, acquisition, conversion, and other business outcomes.
  • Insights & Recommendations: Analyze member, transactional, campaign, digital, and behavioral data to explain performance and identify opportunities, including connecting marketing engagement (e.g., opens, clicks, and views) with application, product, and transactional data to understand downstream behavior, conversion, and business impact.
  • Testing & Experimentation: Design and evaluate A/B tests, control groups, and other approaches to determine the incremental impact of marketing efforts.
  • Member & Audience Analytics: Use segmentation, cohort, funnel, acquisition, retention, and behavioral analysis to improve targeting and understand member response.
  • Analytical Partnership: Serve as Data Services’ primary analytical partner to Marketing, translating business questions into analytical approaches while maintaining independent judgment and professionally challenging conclusions that are not supported by the data.
  • Communication & Storytelling: Present clear, actionable findings to Marketing and leadership, distinguishing between what the data demonstrates, suggests, and cannot establish.
  • Reporting & Visualization: Develop dashboards, scorecards, and recurring reporting that provide meaningful visibility into marketing performance and business impact.
  • Data Quality & Continuous Improvement: Partner with Data Services and Marketing to improve data quality, metric definitions, measurement methodologies, and overall marketing analytics capabilities.

Necessary Experience and Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Business, Analytics, Finance, Mathematics, Statistics, or a related field, or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
  • At least five years of experience in marketing analytics, marketing measurement, customer analytics, or a closely related role.
  • Demonstrated experience analyzing customer or member, transactional, campaign, and behavioral data to measure marketing effectiveness, explain performance, and develop actionable insights and recommendations.
  • Advanced experience writing and optimizing SQL queries, preferably in Snowflake and Oracle.
  • Experience with business intelligence and data visualization tools such as PowerBI.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage and prioritize multiple requests in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong communication skills (written and verbal) with the ability to translate complex analytical findings into clear insights and recommendations for a diverse credit union audience.
  • Demonstrated ability to exercise independent analytical judgment, professionally challenge assumptions, and confidently communicate conclusions supported by data.
  • Experience in financial services or credit unions and an understanding of member, product, and transactional data is preferred.

Work Environment and Physical Requirements

  • Office environment with moderate level of noise
  • Frequent use of telephone, copier, computer, fax machine and other office machines
  • Prolonged sitting or standing
  • Frequent mental and visual concentration
  • Minimal lifting of up to 25 pounds

NOTE: This job has the potential to periodically work remotely contingent upon supervisor approval but is not a work from home eligible position. When working remotely it is necessary to follow our Remote Work / Work from Home Policy.

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of the work being performed in this position. They are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, or requirements.

title: Warehouse Equipment Technician – Mechanical & Production
description:
Warehouse Equipment Technician – Mechanical & Production

Los Angeles, CA | $21/hr + OT | $50K–$52K Estimated Annual Earnings

Looking for a warehouse job where you're actually working with your hands and learning how equipment works?

Auto-Chlor System is hiring a Warehouse Equipment Technician for our Los Angeles team. This isn't a traditional pick-and-pack warehouse position. You'll work hands-on with commercial dishwashing equipment, helping tear down, inspect, repair, clean, and rebuild machines so they're ready to be installed at another customer location.

You'll also support our production and warehouse operation by preparing chemical products, building pallets, receiving shipments, organizing inventory, and operating a sit-down forklift.

If you've worked in warehouse, production, automotive, maintenance, construction, assembly, manufacturing, or another hands-on environment, we'd like to hear from you.

Pay & Schedule

  • $21.00/hour starting pay

  • $50,000–$52,000 estimated annual earnings with anticipated overtime

  • Approximately 4–5 hours of overtime per week

  • 6:30 AM start time

  • Full-time position

  • On-call rotation approximately once every 7–9 weeks

Annual earnings are estimated based on the anticipated overtime schedule. Actual overtime and earnings may vary.

What You'll Be Doing

Equipment Rebuilding

  • Tear down used commercial dishwashing equipment

  • Inspect mechanical components and parts

  • Identify what can be cleaned and reused and what needs to be replaced

  • Replace worn or damaged components

  • Reassemble equipment and prepare it for future installation

  • Perform basic troubleshooting and equipment maintenance

  • Use hand and power tools throughout the rebuilding process

Warehouse & Production

  • Prepare cleaning chemical products

  • Pour and handle chemicals following established safety procedures

  • Build and organize pallets

  • Receive incoming shipments and deliveries

  • Move and organize inventory and equipment

  • Operate a standard sit-down forklift

  • Maintain a clean and organized warehouse

Who We're Looking For

You don't need experience with commercial dishwashing equipment. We'll teach you our equipment and processes.

We're looking for someone who:

  • Enjoys taking things apart and figuring out how they work

  • Is mechanically inclined and comfortable using tools

  • Likes troubleshooting and solving problems

  • Is comfortable performing physical, hands-on work

  • Can balance mechanical projects with warehouse and production responsibilities

  • Is dependable and comfortable with an early morning schedule

  • Is willing to learn new equipment and processes

Sit-down forklift experience is preferred but not required.

Experience in automotive repair, maintenance, construction, HVAC, electrical, manufacturing, assembly, machine operation, warehouse operations, or similar hands-on work can translate well into this position.

Build Your Mechanical Skills

You don't have to already be a mechanic to succeed here.

Maybe you work on your own car. Maybe you've repaired equipment, worked construction, used tools at home, attended trade school, or simply enjoy understanding how machines work.

We're looking for that mechanical curiosity and willingness to learn.

Auto-Chlor System has served the restaurant and hospitality industry since 1938. Join our Los Angeles team and build a long-term career while developing hands-on mechanical, equipment, warehouse, and production experience.

Apply today to be considered.

title: Luxury Jewelry Consultant

title: Field Service Technician
description:
The Field Service Technician I (FST1) is a safety critical position and is responsible for assisting in the manufacture, installation, troubleshooting, and repair of all LB Foster wayside equipment (WILD, Rockfall, Flood Monitoring), ensuring uninterrupted system performance and The Association of American Railroads (AAR) WABL compliance. The FST1 will interact directly with our customers on site, and LB Foster teams: Engineering, Project Management and Operations. title: Mobile Phlebotomist
description:

Pay Range: $18.00-$20.00 Based on experience with Mileage reimbursement

ROLE:

The Mobile Phlebotomist, under the general supervision of the Phlebotomy Supervisor, works to provide clinical pre-analytical laboratory services to our clients/patients in a mobile setting. They are responsible for completing their assigned routes in a safe and timely manner. They must follow all policies and procedures.

• Accurately collects, labels, processes, and delivers specimens obtained from patients.

• Reloads equipment and all necessary specimens to vehicle for prompt delivery.

• Regularly communicates with dispatcher to report status and location.

• Strict adherence to Universal Precautions in controlling blood-borne pathogens and infectious disease exposures.

• Maintain required certifications, health requirements, and operational requirements.

• Keeps work area clean.

• Follow all required safety precautions ALL the time.

• Reports any unsafe conditions in the workplace.

• Reports all complaints and problems encountered.

• Monitors supplies inventory.

• Reports low stock or out-of-stock situations.

• Identifies and segregates any expired supplies

• Reports to work promptly, properly groomed and wears the proper identification at all times when visiting a facility.

• Accurately maintains time records of hours worked and deliver to company as directed.

Manages his/her assigned shift to include meal breaks.

• Follows all specimen preservation, patient preparation and specimen management processes and procedures as written without personal deviation

• Drives vehicle to client facilities (mostly nursing homes), as directed by company dispatcher or assigned supervisor or coordinator.

• Unloads phlebotomy tray provided by the company and takes to patient’s bedside to collect samples for tests ordered by physician.

• Accurately identifies patients before collecting specimens.

• Accurately collects, labels, processes and delivers specimens obtained from patients.

• Reloads equipment and all necessary specimens to vehicle for prompt delivery.

Associates work in all weather and driving conditions.

title: Mammography Technologist
description:
Overview

Who We Are

For nearly 30 years, Women’s Imaging Center (“WIC”) has been Colorado’s most trusted destination for compassionate and specialized women’s imaging care where patients look forward to returning year after year.

Our 4.9 rating across more than 5,000 Google reviews doesn't happen by accident. It happens because of our Team. Many of our technologists, medical assistants, and radiologists have been with us for over 20 years. The care they bring isn’t just professional, it’s personal.

We perform 3D screening and diagnostic mammography, breast ultrasound, MRI, DEXA, and image-guided biopsy often moving from screening to diagnosis within 24 hours. That continuity of care is rare. Our patients feel it, and so will you. You won’t find that elsewhere in Colorado. If you are not familiar with Centennial state, we have over 300 days of sunshine a year, close access to the Rocky Mountains, great education options, and quality of life that consistently rank among the best in the country.

When you join WIC, you're not just filling a role — you're becoming part of a close-knit, experienced group that genuinely loves what they do and feels their talents lie in helping other women.

If you're an experienced mammography technologist who takes pride in the work you do, and do it with expertise and heart, we want to hear from you!

Responsibilities

What Your Days Look Like

We believe the right schedule makes you a better technologist. We work with you to find hours that actually fit your life. And the place you'll spend those hours? Calm, focused, and genuinely upbeat. No hospital noise. No institutional politics. Just good people doing important work. Your day starts the same way every time, making your patients feel seen, respected, and at ease. The next part is dependent on your professional skills, which we are willing to develop or enhance.

On a typical Saturday you might:

  • Guide your patient through the performance of her routine annual screening — answering questions, easing anxiety, and providing information, especially for first time patients.
  • Work up diagnostic exams alongside one of our specialist radiologists, using your positioning expertise and clinical instincts to obtain the optimal imaging for the radiologist's interpretation, working within what is possible (or not) to obtain. This role would be primarly screening patients on a Saturday but we like to keep our options open to do diagnostics as well.
  • Support a patient who is nervous about a callback — your calm, confident presence makes all the difference in how she experiences that moment.
  • Collaborate with a tight-knit team of Technologists, MAs, and Radiologists who genuinely care about your professional development and success.

Your Impact and Growth

Beyond the daily work, there’s room to grow. Let us know what other x-ray skills you have and we can see if you are a good fit for our center.

Show us what you’re capable of.

Qualifications

What We're Looking For

  • ARRT(R)(M) registered — mammography certification required
  • ACR-standard positioning skills you've genuinely practiced and refined
  • 1 or more year(s) of mammography experience preferred. Will consider a motivated new graduate with strong clinical skills.
  • Comfortable with screening and diagnostic workups — somewhere you shine
  • A communicator: with patients, with radiologists, with your Team
  • Someone who sees the person behind every image

Schedule & Locations

Primary locations: Westminster/North (9035 Wadsworth Pkwy #2800, Westminster, CO 80021)

Other available locations: Cherry Creek, Lakewood, and Highlands Ranch

PRN: Must have availability Saturday from 7:00 AM - 2:30 PM (or 3:00 PM). Additional PRN hours available during the week.

Compensation & Benefits

Pay Range: $55 – $62 / hour based on experience

Ready to Join Us?

title: Medicare Billing Specialist

At Care Hospice, we're not just a company; we're a team united by a common goal – providing exceptional hospice and palliative care to those in need. title: Transportation & Logistics Supervisor
description:
Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

Transportation Operations Leadership

  • Directly supervise transportation personnel including drivers and transportation support employees.
  • Plan, prioritize, and oversee daily transportation and dispatch activities.
  • Develop routes, driver schedules and delivery assignments to support operational requirements.
  • Monitor execution of transportation schedules and take corrective action to address service interruptions.
  • Ensure effective utilization of drivers, vehicles, trailers, and transportation resources.
  • Lead daily transportation meetings and communicate operational priorities.
  • Resolve transportation issues impacting customer service, production schedules, or delivery commitments.
  • Recommend and implement transportation process improvements.

Driver Leadership & Performance Management

  • Directly supervise, coach, and develop drivers to ensure safe and efficient performance.
  • Conduct performance reviews, coaching discussions, and corrective action when necessary.
  • Monitor driver productivity, attendance, safety performance, and JJ Keller compliance.
  • Establish clear performance expectations and hold drivers accountable for results.
  • Support recruiting, interviewing, hiring, onboarding, and training activities for transportation personnel.
  • Develop employee skills and succession plans to strengthen transportation operations.
  • Promote a culture of safety, accountability, teamwork, and continuous improvement.

KPI Ownership & Operational Performance

  • Maintain ownership and accountability for transportation-related Key Performance Indicators (KPIs).
  • Manage and report out on SQDEC scorecard for logistics and RMA percentage on a daily basis.
  • Monitor and report transportation performance metrics including:
    • On-Time Delivery
    • Transportation Cost per Load
    • Fleet Utilization
    • Driver Productivity
    • Delivery Accuracy
    • Customer Service Performance
    • Safety Metrics
    • DOT Compliance Metrics
  • Analyze operational data and implement corrective actions when performance goals are not achieved.
  • Utilize reporting and analytics to drive operational improvements and decision-making.
  • Partner with leadership to establish goals and performance targets.

Logistics & Shipping Operations

  • Oversee outbound shipping and logistics activities from order release through customer delivery.
  • Coordinate transportation requirements with Production, Warehouse Operations, and Customer Service teams.
  • Ensure timely movement of finished goods and inventory throughout the distribution process.
  • Monitor shipment execution and resolve customer, supplier, and carrier concerns.
  • Ensure shipping documentation, Bills of Lading, and transportation records are accurately maintained.
  • Verify shipment accuracy and investigate service failures or delivery discrepancies.

Warehouse Systems & Inventory Support

  • Utilize warehouse and ERP systems to manage outbound transactions and inventory movement.
  • Ensure system accuracy and transaction integrity related to transportation and shipping activities.
  • Support inventory control and material flow processes between warehouse and transportation operations.
  • Partner with warehouse leadership to improve workflow efficiency and service performance.
  • Identify opportunities to improve inventory visibility and transportation-related system processes.

Fleet Management & Regulatory Compliance

  • Oversee fleet availability through effective maintenance planning and equipment utilization.
  • Coordinate preventative maintenance schedules and repair activities.
  • Ensure compliance with DOT regulations, driver qualification standards, and Hours of Service requirements.
  • Maintain transportation compliance records through JJ Keller and related systems.
  • Conduct transportation audits and inspections to ensure regulatory compliance.
  • Partner with Safety and Operations leadership to reduce transportation-related risk.

Customer, Vendor & Supplier Management

  • Serve as the primary escalation point for transportation-related customer, supplier, and delivery concerns.
  • Develop strong working relationships with customers, vendors, manufacturing leadership, and warehouse teams.
  • Resolve scheduling conflicts, delivery challenges, and operational disruptions.
  • Ensure professional and proactive communication regarding transportation performance and service levels.

Continuous Improvement

  • Lead transportation initiatives focused on safety, service, efficiency, and cost reduction to include: monthly 6’s initiatives and quarterly Kaizen events.
  • Develop and maintain transportation standard operating procedures.
  • Identify opportunities for automation, technology enhancements, and process optimization.
  • Participate in strategic projects supporting business growth and operational excellence.

Education and Experience

  • Associate's Degree or Bachelor's Degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Transportation, Business Administration, or related field preferred.
  • 3-5 years of transportation, logistics, fleet, distribution, or supply chain experience preferred.
  • Minimum 2 years of leadership or supervisory experience preferred.
  • Experience utilizing ERP, transportation management, fleet management, or warehouse management systems.
  • Working knowledge of DOT regulations and transportation compliance requirements.
  • Demonstrated success leading teams and driving operational performance improvements.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, communication, and leadership skills.

Competencies/ Technical Skills:

  • Customer Focus: Builds strong relationships with internal and external customers while consistently delivering solutions that exceed expectations.
  • Drives Results: Achieves challenging goals through disciplined execution, accountability, and a strong sense of urgency.
  • Learning Agility: Quickly learns new concepts, processes, and technologies while effectively adapting to changing business needs and priorities.
  • Adaptability: Remains effective under pressure, responds constructively to change, and successfully navigates ambiguity and shifting priorities.
  • Building High-Performing Teams: Develops talent, fosters collaboration, and creates an environment where individuals and teams can excel.
  • Problem Solving & Decision Making: Uses data, critical thinking, and sound judgment to solve complex operational challenges and drive sustainable solutions.
  • Communication: Communicates clearly, professionally, and effectively across all levels of the organization.
  • Accountability: Takes ownership of results, holds self and others accountable, and follows through on commitments.
  • Integrity & Trust: Demonstrates honesty, professionalism, and ethical leadership while building credibility and trust throughout the organization.

Work Conditions:

This position operates in both office and manufacturing environments.

  • Regular exposure to moving mechanical equipment, forklifts, and warehouse traffic.
  • Exposure to varying temperatures and manufacturing conditions.
  • Required use of personal protective equipment (PPE), including safety glasses, hearing protection, and steel-toed footwear.
  • Moderate to high noise levels are common in production areas.

Physical Requirements:

The physical requirements described here are representative of those necessary to successfully perform the essential functions of this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • Frequently sit, stand, walk, bend, and move throughout manufacturing and warehouse environments.
  • Ability to occasionally lift and move up to 30 pounds.
  • Ability to operate a computer and other office equipment for extended periods.
  • Ability to visually inspect products, equipment, and work areas.

title: Counselor
description:
Starting Salary: $55,000-$58,000

Hours: 7:30am-3:30pm

Summary

At Pace we transform girls’ lives through academic and counseling programs based on a gender-responsive, strength-based and trauma informed framework. Team members create a safe place for girls to learn, grow, and heal.

The counselor role provides prevention services to girls that includes social emotional support, intensive care (case) management, crisis counseling, and psycho-educational groups to girls. This position is aimed at helping girls decrease risk-related behaviors.

Qualifications and Education Requirements

Required

    • Bachelor's Degree from four-year College or University with a Major in Social Work, Psychology, and Mental Health, Counseling, or a related field

    • Minimum three years prior experience

    • Knowledge of case management practices

    • Excellent individual, group and family counseling and crisis management skills

    • Proficiency in computer skills, database management and/or office software

    • Current Florida driver’s license

    Preferred

    • Master’s Degree; Major in Social Work, Psychology, Mental Health, Counseling or a related field with a minimum of 1-year prior experience

    • Knowledge of laws relating to children and families

    • Experience working with at-risk youth

    • Experience in working in a multidisciplinary team

    Roles and Responsibilities

    Direct Care Services

    • Increase girls’ resiliency and protective factors by improving relationships, increasing self-efficacy, and encouraging self-advocacy

    • Assess and address needs and strengths through holistic assessment, goal setting, and care planning

    • Utilize the Transtheoretical Model of Change, considering any history of trauma and leveraging girls’ strengths

    • Provide bi-weekly counseling services to girls using guidance, support, collaboration, skill acquisition, and psycho-educational services

    • Provide psycho-educational groups that are girl-centered, focusing on social-emotional and life skill development

    • Provide monthly family support/counseling with caregivers to encourage girl progression in the change process and to work with natural supports

    • Provide solution-focused counseling approaches toward the resolution of risk factors for substance abuse following the standards of the Florida Administrative Codes Chapter 65D-30

    • Provide crisis intervention as warranted, including family support, peer mediation, classroom support, and the coordination of risk assessments

    • Provide care (case) management services, including transportation services when needed, field trips and other extracurricular activities, maintain a safe environment in the program, collaborate with outside entities and community providers involved in girls’ care, make referrals as appropriate, and advocate for needed resources

    • Provide strength-based behavior modification and ensure appropriate use of the Growth and Change System, including de-escalation of girls and caregivers when needed

    • Partner with the academic team to ensure holistic, cohesive care

    Non-Direct Care Services, Care Planning, and Monitoring

    • Participate in care review meetings for girls served and provide education to the care planning team using a multidisciplinary framework

    • Collaborate with the intake team to support decision-making about program enrollment

    • Document progress and complete assessments, screening tools, care plans and transition plans

    • Contribute positively toward programmatic outcomes and with the collection of data to support the change process of girls

    • Other duties as assigned

    Other

    • Must adhere to the Pace Center for Girls Values and Guiding Principles and upholds the ethical standards of the Agency

    This position requires a Level II pre-employment background screening pursuant to Chapters 435, 984, 985 and 943, Florida Statutes, and the Department of Juvenile Justice policy and procedures. Additional information is available through the Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse Education and Awareness website: https://info.flclearinghouse.com

title: Senior RF Phased Array Engineer I
description:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

SPACE SYSTEMS

At Rocket Lab, we’re not just launching rockets — we're building the future of space. Our Space Systems team builds everything from complete spacecraft, precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space, like solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, radios, and more.

Our Space Systems team has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration, in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. The team has built spacecraft, payloads, and components for missions to the Moon and Mars, working with partners including NASA, the Space Development Agency, and the U.S. Space Force. Whether it’s a single high-performance spacecraft, constellation, or the vertically integrated components that help them get to space — our world class Space Systems team is empowering some of the boldest and most ambitious space missions.

RF PHASED ARRAY ENGINEER SENIOR I

Based at Rocket Lab's global headquarters in Long Beach, CA, the Senior RF Phased Array Engineer is the technical lead responsible for the development of new RF products and systems (including Rocket Lab’s phased arrays) and assessment of COTS components. The Senior RF Phased Array Engineer will model and simulate antenna performance for current programs and proposals. The successful candidate will have a strong understanding of antennas at the component and system level and will thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.

WHAT YOU'LL GET TO DO:

Product Development

  • Lead end to end efforts including architecture design, prototyping, integration, test, and flight development – Ensure key design decisions and developments are in alignment with product / system needs
  • Model and simulate array performance
  • Lead efforts along side an interdisciplinary team of RF, digital, power, mechanical, thermal, and structural engineers
  • Transition developments from new product introduction to production
  • Interface with vendors and customers
  • Develop test plans and procedures for testing active antennas – included EIRP & G/T
  • Design and development of GSE and production automation
  • Support the development of product documentation including ICDs and User Manuals

Customer/Program Support

  • Drive proposals and requirements specifications to assess compliance based on existing unit capabilities vs development needs
  • Scope and drive development activities for new requirements
  • Support engineering reviews such as PDRs, CDRs and TRRs
  • Provide technical support to internal/external customers including general questions and anomaly troubleshooting
  • Maintain broad awareness of product development and production schedules to ensure the needs of customers and programs are satisfied

YOU'LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS AS SENIOR RF PHASED ARRAY ENGINEER I:

  • Bachelors degree in electrical engineering, RF communications (or an equivalent qualification) and 5+ years of relevant experience
  • Fundamental RF knowledge including link budget analysis and linearity.
  • A solid theoretical and practical understanding of RF communications and navigation systems and components
  • Experience running modeling and simulation of antenna / phased array performance.
  • Deep understanding of the effects of interference on the system
  • Experience in developing and delivering a RF system including assessing requirements, prototyping engineering models, and producing space worthy products.

THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE:

  • Extensive experience in space grade system design
  • Extensive experience in analyses including worst case, reliability, FMECA, thermal, and derating analyses
  • Extensive experience supporting and leading complex engineering programs and developing associated documentation
  • Experience designing, integrating, and testing RF communications systems for launch vehicles or satellites
  • Demonstrated expertise in mentoring others.
  • Experience leading incident management and investigations.
  • Experience in conflict resolution and dealing with difficult people.
  • The ability to work under pressure and to tight deadlines
  • Effective communication skills and the ability to build strong working relationships
  • Project management experience

This position may require prolonged periods of sitting, standing, walking, computer work, and occasional exposure to moderate levels of noise, dust, and fumes in production areas.

Anticipated annual equity grant value is designed around function, level, experience, and other factors; realized value depends on vesting and stock-price performance.

Join one of the world's fastest-growing space companies and own a piece of it. In addition to competitive base pay, you'll receive company stock as part of your total compensation package, giving you a direct stake in our success. As we expand to new launch sites, groundbreaking missions, and global markets, your ownership has the opportunity to grow alongside the company.

Our comprehensive benefits package includes our industry-leading Employee Stock Purchase Program (with a 15% discount on company stock), top-tier medical plans (HMO, PPO, and a zero cost HDHP option with a significant HSA company contribution), dental and vision coverage, paid vacation and sick time, 11 paid holidays, flexible spending and dependent care accounts, paid parental leave, disability and life insurance, and a 401(k) retirement plan with company match.

We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. title: In-line Inspection MFL/GEO Data Analyst (Level 2-3)
description:
Onstream Pipeline Inspection is a leading provider of Inline and Tethered Magnetic Flux Leakage, Caliper, and Inertial Measurement inspection services for oil and gas pipeline operators across North America.

The In-line Inspection MFL/GEO Data Analyst (Level 2-3) will evaluate and interpret pipeline inspection data collected by Onstream’s MFL (Magnetic Flux Leakage) and Geometry inline inspection tools . You will correlate analysis with field verification measurements, perform QA/QC checks, generate detailed customer survey reports, and interface directly with clients .

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES/ACTIVITIES:

  • Data Analysis & Interpretation: Interpret MFL and Geometry pipeline inspection data to identify anomaly locations, depth, and categorization on oil and gas pipelines .

  • Quality Assurance & Verification: Perform data quality assessments, run standard/non-standard analyses, apply anomaly interaction rules, and conduct final QA/QC checks on completed survey reports .

  • Historical & Field Correlation: Correlate findings with historical inspection data and physical, hands-on measurements taken from client-provided corrosion samples .

  • Reporting & Client Interaction: Generate and present final inspection reports tailored to client specifications . Provide ongoing technical support to clients via phone, email, and in-person for excavations and measurement verification .

  • Technical Leadership (Level 3): Establish analysis techniques/procedures, interpret industry codes and standards, perform advanced analysis, and mentor/train junior team members

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS:

  • Experience: 5+ years of equivalent inline inspection MFL/GEO data analysis experience .

  • Certifications: Historical or active Level 2 or Level 3 MFL/GEO certification .

  • Education: Minimum of 2 years completed engineering or science coursework at a recognized college, technical school, or university (or an additional 2 years of equivalent industry experience) .

  • Industry Standards: Advanced working knowledge of PHMSA Part 192/195 regulations, as well as API, NACE, and ASME standards and recommended practices .

  • Driver’s License: Valid driver’s license (required for occasional client visits and meetings) .

  • Preferred Asset: Experience and training in non-destructive testing (NDT) .

  • Strong computer, analytical, and data interpretation skills .

  • Ability to learn proprietary software and technical concepts quickly .

  • Self-motivated and able to work with minimal supervision while meeting deadlines .

  • High attention to detail with the ability to maintain concentration over long periods .

  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills for team collaboration and professional client presentations

title: Yacht Division Product Specialist
description:
OVERVIEW:

The Yacht Support Product Specialist is an integral part of the growth strategy and focus for the Yacht Division. The Yacht Support Product Specialist will be responsible for being a liaison to our teams as well as creating and delivering customer experience the drives a next level of confidence for our customers and the team. The growth & development of the Yacht Division requires that our valuable customers, retail locations and dealers are educated and supported at a high level.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Enthusiastically embrace MarineMax values
  • Acquire complete product knowledge of all Yacht Division models from all perspectives.
  • Work with Yacht Support and service teams to provide technical support to customers, technicians, service support, service managers and sales.
  • Embrace utilization of the MarineMax digital platform for all communication.
  • Collaborate with all team members, stakeholders, and dealer network to execute cohesive roll out campaigns for educational initiatives for our customers of the yacht division.
  • Collaborate with team on common issues for the manufacturer and work with Yacht Support to present a clear concise packet of information to the manufacturer to ensure issues are resolved or refined on future boats.
  • Work closely with teams to tailor existing delivery documentation and refined specifically for yacht deliveries.
  • Strategize with Yacht Support, Service Manager, National Warranty Manager to develop a gallery of training videos, how-to videos, and educational pieces for our customers.
  • Support teams at regional boat shows and customer events.
  • Maintain a professional and supportive relationship with all clients, fellow team members, vendors, and the manufacturers.
  • Participate in and be a leader for getaways and yacht division customer events.
  • Assist Yacht Support and stores to always maintain FANS Scores of 80% or higher for the Yacht Division.
  • Support and work on all other tasks deemed necessary to the team’s success.

REQUIREMENTS:

  • International and domestic travel required
  • Some weekends and after hours support necessary
  • Captains license a plus

The role works closely with the entire network of locations working with Yacht Support and assist with the roll-out of these initiatives to MarineMax stores and related Yacht Division business units.
